params.body:
Closes #473

## Why

What Gentells reads from Belgium is thin. The coverage read of 19 November 2026 shows 115 Belgian sources known and 9 read. Half of the Belgian signals of the last 90 days come from one broadcaster and a third from search trends. Nothing French-language is read, and none of the music, culture, gaming and lifestyle titles young people in Belgium read is on any list.

## What

A fourth source list, `research/source-list-2026-11-19.json`: 29 Belgian titles with a live feed that none of the three earlier lists holds, refs `GT-M62-01` to `GT-M62-29`.

- **14 Dutch-language:** Bruzz, Het Laatste Nieuws, Het Nieuwsblad, Humo, Newsmonkey, Enola, Indiestyle, Dansende Beren, Knack Focus, Knack Weekend, Flair, Elle België, 4Gamers, Sporza.
- **15 French-language:** RTBF Info, La Libre Belgique, La Dernière Heure, L'Avenir, 7sur7, Moustique, Le Vif, Focus Vif, Le Vif Weekend, Paris Match Belgique, Flair, Elle Belgique, Le Suricate Magazine, Mammouth, Scan-R.

The list is read by the same `bin/import-source-list.mjs`. Every row comes in `proposed` and inactive: nothing is read until a person starts a trial, and nothing is cited until a person admits it.

Each feed was fetched on 19 November 2026 and answered with items dated in the last week, except Scan-R (last item 16 November, one in the week). Priority A marks the titles made by or for young people (Indiestyle, Dansende Beren, Mammouth, Scan-R) and RTBF Info as the counterpart of VRT NWS; C marks the high-volume general and sport titles, where most items will not be about young people.

## Choices

- **Region.** All rows are at home in `region-belgium` (Standard 0.19.0). The language tells the Dutch- and French-language titles apart.
- **A new type label, `Nieuwsmedium`,** for general news titles. The earlier lists had no such row; the label is kept in the listing only and no code reads it.
- **Left out on purpose:** De Morgen (the pipeline holds it as `src-demorgen`, inactive, at an address that no longer answers a feed; its feed moved to `/rss.xml`, a repair rather than a new source); the French and English editions of VRT NWS (translations of what is already read); De Standaard, Le Soir, Sudinfo, BX1 and GrenzEcho (their feeds refuse a reader, 403); titles whose feed went quiet (Subbacultcha, Gonzo Circus, Alter Echos, Wilfried, Médor).
- **Not solved here:** Belgian titles without a feed (StampMedia, Veto, dwars, MO*, Chase, Tagmag, Kifkif), and observed signals from platforms. Press counts as reported; a trend still needs observed signals to reach the site.

## Checked

- `test/source-lifecycle.test.mjs`: a new case reads the list on top of the three earlier lists and the Belgian sources read before any list (VRT NWS, Knack, De Morgen): 29 added, none labelled, none twice, all `rss` at their own feed, all proposed and inactive, at home in Belgium, 14 `nl` and 15 `fr`.
- None of the 29 sites is held on production today, looked up by host. Knack Focus and Knack Weekend sit under Knack's site and have their own feed.
- Full suite 1748/1748, `tsc` clean.

## After merge, on the box

```bash
node bin/import-source-list.mjs research/source-list-2026-11-19.json           # dry: expect 29 new, proposed
node bin/import-source-list.mjs research/source-list-2026-11-19.json --apply
```

The 29 then wait as proposals beside the 24 Belgian sources already waiting. Starting trials is the desk's work, on the Sources page or through Ask; a first wave of the A and B rows is a sensible start.

The high-volume feeds (La Libre, La Dernière Heure, L'Avenir, Moustique, Paris Match hand out 100 items at a time) will raise intake and classification cost during the trial; the scorecard after two weeks says which earn their place.
params.title: A source list of 29 Belgian feeds, Dutch- and French-language
